summary: Closed two trust-boundary gaps in the deterministic-replay research path. First, the previous beta-binomial fresh-process screen was recognized as relying on a common Bernoulli mismatch parameter and was superseded for general issuance by a precommitted fixed-horizon Hoeffding-Azuma screen that targets the average conditional mismatch rate under heterogeneous/adaptive bounded fresh-process trials. Second, the replay bootstrap was changed from merely pinning a certificate digest to pinning and semantically rechecking an immutable certificate record, issuance-gate blob, trust-provider blob, runtime blob, and lifetime spending contract before constructing the v5 RuntimeContext. No default runtime was switched; FAIL_CLOSED remains the safe path.

new_measurement_validity_finding.name: common-p-certification-is-too-strong-an-assumption
new_measurement_validity_finding.finding: The v1 beta-binomial mixture screen is valid under a common conditional Bernoulli mismatch parameter p, but fresh-process challenge mismatch can vary by attempt/runtime covariates. It must not be generalized to heterogeneous/adaptive challenge streams merely because each observation is binary.
new_measurement_validity_finding.repair: V2 precommits the challenge horizon and uses the one-sided bounded martingale/Hoeffding-Azuma bound Xbar + sqrt(log(1/alpha)/(2n)) for the running average of conditional mismatch probabilities. Optional stopping is not authorized in this screen.
new_measurement_validity_finding.scope: This certifies only an average conditional mismatch-rate bound over the challenge protocol. It is still not proof of exact determinism or a worst-case per-input guarantee; structural exactness attestation remains mandatory.

trial_unit_guards: each challenge has a distinct attempt_id
the two fresh process identifiers within a pair differ
process identifiers cannot be reused across challenge trials
observed challenge count must equal the precommitted fixed horizon

checks: manifest and every authority artifact are Git-blob verified
certificate id/digest/structural-attestation digest must match manifest
issuance gate blob must match certificate record
zero mismatch and exact precommitted horizon are required
A/[j(j+1)] generation alpha is rederived and compared with evidence
fixed-horizon upper bound must not exceed tolerance
certificate payload digest and its runtime/evidence/policy bindings are rederived
provider registry and runtime snapshot must match the evidence-bound certificate record
evidence_bound_bootstrap_v2.algorithmic_negative_control: A semantically modified certificate record with the reported upper bound changed above tolerance was rejected even when the outer record digest and manifest bindings were recomputed in the local fixture.
evidence_bound_bootstrap_v2.byte_execution_limit: The private v5 transitive graph is not materialized into the local Python filesystem by the connector in this invocation, so the new bootstrap loader was validated algorithmically with a stub RuntimeContext rather than full v5 byte-execution. Earlier checkpoint separately byte-executed v5 and its transitive replay graph.

revisions: determinism_certificate_issuance_gate_v1_2026_08_28.py and its v1 certificate are superseded for general heterogeneous challenge issuance; retain only under an explicitly common conditional Bernoulli mismatch model.
The first bootstrap v1 only pinned a certificate digest and is superseded by v2, which binds and semantically rechecks the certificate record and fixed-horizon issuance contract.
Two serialization mistakes in early v1 trust-provider/manifest drafts were detected by Git blob readback and corrected before v2 was built; no v1 artifact was promoted to active runtime.

A single GitHub create_file returned a transient 409 because main advanced concurrently; the identical authorized role-local write was retried successfully. No control semantics were refetched or adopted after the semantic-freeze barrier.
scope_limitations: No default/active runtime was switched. DETERMINISTIC_REPLAY remains a research candidate; FAIL_CLOSED remains the safe active path.
The v2 certificate is for a toy deterministic hash-style score fixture, not an LLM runtime determinism certificate.
The v2 trust provider is a static parameterless fixture, not a live runtime fingerprint/invalidation attestor.
The statistical screen bounds average conditional mismatch under its challenge protocol; it cannot by itself establish exact replay equivalence or worst-case input determinism.

The structural attestation is currently represented by a digest in the certificate record. The bootstrap does not yet pin and re-execute an independently stored proof artifact plus raw challenge transcript; a privileged manifest author could still pin a fabricated internally consistent certificate record.
Full new-bootstrap-to-v5 byte-execution was not possible in the local Python filesystem this invocation because connector files are not mounted there.
frontier: Persist and pin the full structural-attestation artifact and raw fresh-process challenge transcript, then have the bootstrap rerun the pinned v2 issuance gate from those raw inputs instead of trusting an internally consistent certificate record.

Materialize the exact v5 transitive graph plus bootstrap v2 into one execution filesystem and byte-execute bootstrap -> RuntimeContext -> authorized replay end to end, including tampered record/provider/runtime negative controls.

Replace the static runtime-snapshot fixture with a verified live provider whose implementation and environment fingerprint are themselves content-addressed and whose invalidation state cannot be caller-supplied.

For a real LLM protected statistic, design challenge sampling so the average-conditional mismatch estimand has deployment meaning; keep worst-case or rare-stratum guarantees separate from average mismatch certification.
Only after the above evidence and live-provider checks should DETERMINISTIC_REPLAY be compared against FAIL_CLOSED on wall latency/compute; do not enable replay from the toy certificate.
exact_continuation: Next run: build an immutable structural-attestation artifact and a raw challenge-transcript artifact for the toy protected statistic, bind both by Git blob in a bootstrap-v3 manifest, and make bootstrap-v3 rerun determinism_certificate_issuance_gate_v2 from those raw inputs to reproduce the certificate digest. Include a negative control that fabricates a certificate record while leaving raw transcript/proof unchanged and require bootstrap rejection. Then, if filesystem materialization is available, run the resulting bootstrap against exact v5 bytes rather than a stub RuntimeContext.

termination.reason: Substantive statistical-scope correction, certificate-issuance hardening, and evidence-bound bootstrap work were persisted. The next gap is raw-proof/transcript provenance and full bootstrap-to-v5 byte-execution, not further extension of the current certificate-record-only layer.
